newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher on Menem kudos.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher on Menem kudos.

text.p: Argentine stocks resumed their cautious advance Thursday with good reviews for President Carlos Menem's strident pep talk to Peronist leaders, dealers said.
"The market is clearly reflecting this," said Rafael Aldazabal of brokers Aldazabal. "There is a new sense the president is back again managing the country's economy."
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.9 percent to 521.08, wiping out Wednesday's slim loss to stand 2.3 percent higher so far in the week.

Menem launched a strong appeal to Peronists gathered Thursday for a summit at the Olivos presidential residence, urging them to close ranks against "the enemy at the door" and seeking support for labor reforms.
The fiery speech was expected to motivate Congress to pass a controversial package of tax legislation this month.
In recent weeks speculation the president was losing his clout and would see the tax reforms stall in Congress had dogged the markets.
"Today's speech shows Menem is in fact gaining power," said Jose Napoli of traders Ignoto y Napoli.
"There's been a change of mood since last week. People may not be feeling it yet but we feel it in the markets, especially in bonds," said Aldazabal.
The fear of a sudden jump Friday in U.S. long bond yields, however, kept a lid on the bolsa and caused some speculative selling at the close, traders said.
"Investors can't avoid being on their guard. If U.S. jobs data comes in strong tomorrow many may dump positions anticipating a Federal Reserve rate hike," said Napoli.
In the session floor volume remained weak but picked up to 16 million pesos from 12.5 million Wednesday.
Over-the-counter deals grew to 66.9 million pesos from 57.4 million Wednesday.
The broad market advanced 0.4 percent, with winners outstripping losers 32 to 12 and 19 issues closing flat.

The day's main-tier standout was petrochemical firm Ipako, which soared 13.7 percent after reporting a yearly $92.1 million profit and announcing its merger with holding company Garovaglio, a second-line stock, which surged 10 percent.
Beleaguered Pepsi bottler Baesa, a second-line issue, also shot up 10 percent amid rumors of a new bailout plan by PepsiCo.
Sharpest MerVal losers were Bansud bank and construction stock Polledo, both off 2.2 percent, steelmaker Siderca, which dropped 1.2 percent, and carmaker Sevel, down 1.0 percent.
